ratings_why.fun: Two clear ways to grow, a fight Procession and a shop Wake, both running on one word, and a slot that refills bigger is satisfying to watch.
ratings_why.distinct: Folding sale into death is fresh, but Sprouts that refill on death sit close to familiar Deathrattle and Reborn tribes.

verdict_why: The Sprout, the card every other card reads, has unclear stats, and that is a real fix.

points.text: Sprout's X/X can't be read: is it fixed when it is summoned or does it keep growing, and what is a recruit Sprout's size in the next fight once 'this turn' ends? Say 'X/X, where X is the count when it was summoned' if that is meant.
Clerk Inkcap's 'permanently loses 1 Health' in a fight has no clear meaning; say whether fight losses carry over to the shop.
'Twice a turn' and 'last turn' on Hired Mute and Ludwig don't say whether the fight is part of the turn; one line in the keyword would settle it for the whole tribe.
Old Fingers depends on a hidden history; show the last two non-Sprout units laid to rest beside the Register so a player can see what he will dig up.
The fantasy lands in the cards (Inkcap writing himself away, Ludwig refusing to leave, the Register); Crape Spinner and Lamplighter are plain auras that could do something funereal instead.

standouts.why: Clerk Inkcap is the brief's character in one line: he buffs others and writes himself shorter until he dies.
Ludwig 'can't be sold' is the lodger who won't leave, and it reads at a glance.
Candlesnuff Abbess is a short, readable capstone that turns the front row into a procession.

weakest.why: Crape Spinner is a generic Sprout aura with no Guild flavour in what it does.
Foxfire Lamplighter overlaps Crape Spinner and Bootlace as a third Sprout buffer.
Sexton buffs the shop off a count the player must track; useful but hard to feel.

flags.note: Sprout stats: fixed at summon or live, and what recruit Sprouts become next fight.
Permanent Health loss inside a fight is undefined.
With Bootlace Cordwainer, six Fruit triggers make twelve Sprouts a fight; long chains may read as noise.
Bellows with Cordwainer and Pallbearer in the shop sell loop, as the designer says; worth a sim.
